description: Upstream updates arrive as reviewable pull requests (K5, ruling 7bg.5). Renovate and not Dependabot because it
runs on GitHub and on Forgejo, and this project's forge is not a settled thing; nothing below is a GitHub-only
feature, so this file moves with the repository.
Checking this file in does not start it: a person with admin on the account must install the app or stand up
the self-hosted runner once. Until that happens the lock is deterministic and unwatched, which is a narrower
gap than an unpinned one but still a gap.

dockerfile.description: deploy/Containerfile.store is not named Dockerfile; without this the two base images are unseen.

packageRules.description: Actions are pinned to a commit, and Renovate keeps the trailing version comment honest.
The OpenTelemetry API, SDK and exporter are released together upstream; splitting them across three PRs would propose combinations nobody ships.
The green bar's own tools land as one reviewable change, since they are reviewed by the bar itself going green.
A base-image digest bump is a rebuild and a restart of every tenant's store; it is never grouped with anything else.

uv is a build-stage tool that never reaches the runtime layer, and it is referenced twice: as the version input to setup-uv in the workflows and as the image the Containerfile copies the binary from. They move together, so CI and the image always build with the same uv [K5c, 2026-09-05: the first run proposed them as two PRs].

The version input to setup-uv is a release number, not an action ref. Pinning it to a commit is meaningless and failed on every run (the Repository Problems entry on the first dashboard). Digest pinning stays on for every real action.

The runtime Python is ruled, not maintained: 3.12 is the floor the distributions declare and the version the container ships (owner, 2026-09-04). Digest bumps of 3.12-slim still arrive, because those are the base being rebuilt underneath us; a move to another Python is a decision and never a PR.
